body:
Thanks for the input. I've thought a little about this, here's my thoughts.

> It can easily be assumed that use_fixed_seed makes each run of the particles identical.

I think that fixed seed not causing particle loops to behave the same is expected behaviour, at least for the target audience of particles (works like this in other engines too), so I don't think it needs to be documented. Note that I plan to add an option to force particle subsequential loops to behave exactly the same, to make it possible to create animated sprites out of particles.

> Setting seed still works regardless of the value of use_fixed_seed. It also doesn't clarify that seed is only effective if assigned before starting emitting, if set after nothing happens.

We go into semantics here, but what does it mean, for a general user, to "work". If setting it with random seed set to true works only in a weird combo with `restart(true)`, then it doesn't really "work". It's more that there is an edge usecase that makes it work.

> The documentation for [GPUParticles2D.use_fixed_seed](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_gpuparticles2d.html#class-gpuparticles2d-property-use-fixed-seed) and [GPUParticles3D.use_fixed_seed](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_gpuparticles3d.html#class-gpuparticles3d-property-use-fixed-seed) is also a bit incomplete, and should probably clarify that this does not affect the seed when particles loop, only when reset with restart

Setting seed will affect subsequent loops of an already started particle system.

I think that it doesn't hurt to document the behavior here and what is expected, changing the seed after the particles have started does nothing and requires you to `restart` or emit them again, which I think is easily confusing to people using it with no prior experience. It might be less confusing that emitting particles with `amount == 1` and not `one_shot` isn't looping but just emitting randomly, but it can easily be confusing if there's no clarification what individual terms used are, i.e. what is a "replay" and what is a "session". I don't think that some clarification would hurt.

> Setting seed will affect subsequent loops of an already started particle system.

Already started particles won't respect a change in `seed` until `restart` is called, see the MRP

I think it can be a bit obscure that things behave differently when setting `one_shot = true` and restarting manually or emitting manually and not, at least it was for me getting into using particles for the first time
Oh I agree oneshot is confusing, but I have plans to nuke that into orbit for good and replace it with better emission options
